about: Prosthetics Hero is a working reference for a health or wellbeing product: the hero section laid out, measured and ready to rebuild. The palette is white #FDFCFC underneath. The entry names the stack that produced the page (React and Tailwind CSS) rather than hiding it. The page keeps its motion to 200ms transitions. If you are briefing a health hero section, start from this composition and replace the subject.

layout.title: The bar shares the page grid
layout.body: The bar is one row of text and one action, measured at type from 12px to 14px and 13px spacing steps so it reads as a strip rather than as a band. The bar sits over the 640x464 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: The announcement pill
layout.body: A single pill carries the announcement above the headline, and nothing else competes for that position. It is positioned so the headline keeps the centre of the composition. One badge, one message.

layout.title: A navigation bar that gets out of the way
layout.body: Focus and hover states are specified for each link rather than inherited from the browser. Give the wordmark no more room than its type needs.

layout.title: Measured, not eyeballed
layout.body: Sizes are quoted rather than inherited: type from 12px to 14px, 13px spacing steps and 200ms transitions. Swap the face or the copy and those relationships still hold. The list is short enough that a reviewer can check it element by element.

motion.title: A small interactive surface
motion.body: Every interactive element does one thing (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card), which is what keeps the states predictable. Nothing on the page opens a modal or hijacks the scroll; the interactions stay local to the element.

motion.title: Timings in milliseconds
motion.body: Hover, press and focus all resolve in 200ms, which is what makes the interface feel immediate. Every state change names a value, so the browser default is never used.

fonts.name: Face not specified
fonts.role: The brief fixes the type scale but leaves the face to the build

editorial.title: The numbers behind the hero section
editorial.body: The hero section is measured, not eyeballed. type from 12px to 14px and 13px spacing steps come from the brief, and the layout is arranged to those steps rather than nudged into place. Nothing in this hero section depends on a default.

editorial.title: What a health or wellbeing product gains here
editorial.body: The trade-off is density: this hero section says less on the first screen than a feature-led layout would. What it keeps is the reading order, and navigation, the headline, the announcement badge and the background clip do the work a longer page would spread out. Prosthetics Hero states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: How Prosthetics Hero sequences the first read
editorial.body: Set your own copy into this hero section and the sequence still holds, because the elements are not interchangeable: navigation, the headline, the announcement badge and the background clip each carry one job. A health reader gets the offer before the options.

faq.question: How much of Prosthetics Hero depends on React and Tailwind CSS?
faq.answer: Prosthetics Hero was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: How do the 200ms transitions in Prosthetics Hero behave?
faq.answer: The motion is specified at the same level of detail as the layout: state changes settle in the 200ms range. Port the composition first and the timings second, because they are easier to match once the layout holds.
